title: Rambali v. State of U.P.
coram: Siddhartha Varma, J.; Dr. Yogendra Kumar Srivastava, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; representation under cl. 6.5 to be decided in one month.
headnote: A demand notice of Rs.1,03,226 on a connection alleged to have been disconnected in 1994 is to be objected before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed with a time-bound direction to consider the representation.
facts: Petitioner Rambali challenged a notice issued by the electricity authorities directing deposit of Rs.1,03,226 against Connection No. 5974069000. He contended that the connection had been disconnected in 1994 and that the bills were therefore erroneous. The Electricity Department submitted that the grievance had an efficacious remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Counsel for the petitioner did not dispute that remedy.

holding_units.holding: A consumer disputing a demand notice as erroneously raised on a long-disconnected connection must first approach the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5; the High Court will not decide the billing objection on writ and will instead direct time-bound consideration of a representation.

not_decided.point: Whether the demand of Rs.1,03,226 on Connection No. 5974069000 was erroneous because the connection was disconnected in 1994
not_decided.note: Left to the Executive Engineer on the petitioner's representation under Clause 6.5.
